title: Incident sandbox simulator and safe mock-runner
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: On-call runbooks and replay tooling are valuable for training and post-incident validation but previous replay utilities at Redwood risked noisy side effects (outbound webhooks, alert fog, metric skew). This PR implements an 'incident sandbox simulator' and a 'safe mock-runner' that lets responders replay recorded incident traces against candidate runbooks and automations in an isolated environment with configurable side-effect policies. High level: adds a sandbox runner service that replays events and telemetries, a mock external connector layer with strict allowlist/denylist and response stubbing, and a traffic-shaping timewarp that lets teams speed up or slow down traces for long-running incidents. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked ENG-2189 summarizing safety model and policies - [x] Sandbox service + CLI to start ephemeral run - [x] Mock connector interface and adapters for PagerDuty, Slack, Metrics, and internal webhook endpoints - [x] Timewarp + deterministic clock for replay - [x] E2E tests and CI job for the sandbox runner - [x] Documentation updates and quickstart example Usage summary: run "inc-sandbox start --trace-id <id> --policy deny-all --timewarp 100x" to launch an ephemeral environment that replays telemetry and executes runbook steps without touching production endpoints. The mock-runner supports three safety modes: deny-all (no external calls), stubbed (pre-seeded responses), and shadow (send but tag and discard results), plus a dry-run output-only mode. Commits: - initial scaffold for sandbox service and CLI (inc-sandbox) - add connector abstraction and PagerDuty/Slack stubs - implement timewarp and deterministic clock - tests: trace fixtures and CI e2e harness - docs: quickstart and safety-model writeup Changed files (high level): incident-bot/cmd/inc-sandbox/main.go incident-bot/internal/sandbox/service.go incident-bot/internal/sandbox/runner.go incident-bot/internal/sandbox/connector_stub.go incident-bot/internal/sandbox/timewarp.go incident-bot/test/fixtures/traces/ longrunning-oom.trace incident-bot/test/e2e/sandbox_e2e_test.go docs/sandbox-quickstart.md docs/sandbox-safety.md Key implementation notes: the sandbox runs as a separate binary to avoid accidental production hooks, uses a plugin-based connector registry so teams can add safe adapters for new integrations, and stores ephemeral state in a namespaced in-memory store with optional persistence to a local temp file for replay debugging. The timewarp multiplies wall-clock intervals and advances a deterministic monotonic clock used throughout the runner to ensure timing-sensitive automations behave reproducibly. Review thread summary: Ethan: "Overall good direction. Two requests: tighten the default denylist and add a warning when stubbed mode is used in CI." Response (Maya): "Agree, tightened denylist and added an explicit CI guard; stubbed mode requires opt-in via sandbox.allow_stubbed_in_ci in CI config." Priya: "Can we add an adapter that simulates rate-limited 429 responses to validate backoff logic?" Response: "Added a test adapter and a trace fixture that injects synthetic 429 bursts; documented how to enable in quickstart." Diego: "Make sure the deterministic clock doesn't leak into production libs." Response: "Sandbox-only clock is namespaced and not exported; added linter check to prevent accidental import into core runtime." CI: The new sandbox_e2e job runs in a hermetic container with network disabled; initial CI run failed due to a flaky timewarp edge case, fixed in follow-up commit that stably passes in current pipeline. Migration and rollout: this is an opt-in developer tool. Configuration defaults to disabled in on-call clusters; quickstart shows how to run locally or in a dedicated ephemeral namespace. Backwards compatibility: no changes to runtime or production connectors. Release notes: Adds an incident sandbox and safe mock-runner for replaying incident traces in an isolated environment. Known limitations: current Slack/PagerDuty stubs do not emulate all edge cases such as enterprise SSO redirects; future work tracked ENG-2245 will add richer stubs and a library of synthetic fault injections. Related: incident postmortem toolkit and on-call training examples. Merge outcome: merged via squash after approvals and a passing CI run. This PR is intended to reduce risk when validating runbook changes and to provide a reproducible playground for on-call exercises.
